title: Watt, Horsepower, BTU/h, Ton: The Power Units of HVAC and Motors
h1: Power units — watt, horsepower, BTU/h and refrigeration ton
description: 1 hp = 746 W. 1 ton refrigeration = 12 000 BTU/h = 3.517 kW. Same physical quantity, four different sales sheets.

author.name: The Turbo Unit Converter engineering desk

reviewer.name: Turbo Unit Converter editorial review
reviewer.credential: verified against NIST SP 811 and category-specific ISO references

hero: Motor nameplate in hp, HVAC in BTU/h or tons, everything electrical in W. Convert once — do not stack rounded factors.
body: Power is energy per time. Every industry that sells motors or air conditioners picked its own unit. The ratios are not friendly numbers.

> 1 hp (mechanical) = 745.7 W
> 1 hp (metric, PS) = 735.5 W
> 1 BTU/h = 0.2931 W
> 1 ton refrigeration = 12 000 BTU/h = 3517 W
> 1 kW = 1.341 hp = 3412 BTU/h
Watt / kW: electrical, universal SI. hp: US motors, automotive, pumps. PS / metric hp: European automotive. BTU/h: US HVAC, boilers. Ton: commercial refrigeration and AC.

Old 3-ton AC = 36 000 BTU/h = 10.55 kW cooling. At SEER 14, electrical input at full load ≈ 10.55/(14/12) × 1000 ≈ 9040 W ≈ 12.1 hp electrical (nameplate). A '5 hp' condensing unit at 3.7 kW is only good for 1 ton — sized wrong by 3×.
hp ~ 746 W. Ton = 3.5 kW. BTU/h × 0.293 = W.

faqs.a: Different by 1.4%. PS (Pferdestärke) is 735.5 W; hp is 745.7 W. Car spec sheets swap them casually.
The heat needed to melt one short ton of ice in 24 hours — a real historical reference to ice-based refrigeration.
